title: Extending Your Stay in Thailand: Exemption, Tourist Visa, DTV and More
summary: Most stays in Thailand can be extended once at an immigration office with form TM7 and a 1,900 THB fee. Visa-exempt and tourist visa stays usually get 30 more days. DTV holders can get up to 180 more days per entry. Long-stay visas extend by up to a year if you meet the rules.
seoTitle: Thailand Visa Extension: TM7, 1,900 THB Fee and What You Can Get
seoDescription: How to extend your stay at a Thai immigration office: 30 days for visa exemption and tourist visas, 180 days for DTV, 1 year for retirement or marriage, documents and the 1,900 THB fee.

sections.heading: How extensions work
paragraphs: An extension of stay adds time to the permission-to-stay date stamped in your passport. You apply in person at the immigration office that covers your address, before your current date runs out.
The fee is 1,900 THB per application, whatever your visa type. The form is TM7.

sections.heading: What you can usually get
list: Visa exemption: one extension of up to 30 days. From 15 September 2026, most eligible nationalities get 30 days on entry, down from 60.
Tourist visa (TR): 60 days on entry, then one extension of up to 30 days.
Destination Thailand Visa (DTV): 180 days per entry, then one extension of up to 180 days.
Non-Immigrant O retirement: up to 1 year, if you meet the 800,000 THB or 65,000 THB a month rule.
Non-Immigrant O marriage or family: up to 1 year, if you meet the 400,000 THB or 40,000 THB a month rule.
Business (Non-B) and education (Non-ED): up to 1 year, based on your job or school, with letters from your employer or school.

sections.heading: Documents to bring
list: Your passport, plus copies of the photo page, visa, latest entry stamp and any previous extension
Proof of address, such as a TM30 receipt or hotel booking
For long-stay extensions: the extra documents for your category, such as a bank letter, marriage certificate or employer letter

sections.heading: Step by step
list: Find the immigration office for the province where you live. In Bangkok that's the Government Complex on Chaeng Watthana Road.
Go early with all documents and copies. Many offices use a queue ticket system.
Hand in your documents, pay 1,900 THB and wait for your passport.
Check the new permission-to-stay date before you leave.

sections.heading: When to apply
paragraphs: Apply before your current permission to stay ends. For short extensions, a week before is sensible. For 1-year extensions, many offices accept applications from about 30 days before your date. Ask your office.

sections.heading: If you can't extend
paragraphs: If you don't qualify, or you've already used your extension, you must leave by your permission-to-stay date. Overstaying leads to a 500 THB-a-day fine and possible entry bans.

faqs.q: How much does an extension cost?
faqs.a: 1,900 THB per application, paid at the immigration office.

faqs.q: Can I extend a visa exemption more than once?
faqs.a: Normally no. You get one extension of up to 30 days. After that you must leave or get a different visa.

faqs.q: Can I extend in any province?
faqs.a: Apply at the immigration office that covers the address where you are staying.

faqs.q: Can an agent extend for me?
faqs.a: You normally need to go in person. Someone can apply for you only in special cases, such as a hospital stay with a doctor's certificate.

faqs.q: Do I need a TM30 receipt?
faqs.a: Many offices ask for proof that your address was reported (TM30). Ask your landlord or hotel for it before you go.
